about: Starting presets for Talk Timer. Henry can edit, add and delete them in the app; his changes are saved on the phone. 'Restore starting timers' brings these back. Each starting preset has "rules": slides shown by the Rules button (from Henry's lesson slides; the Fix It! Pitch ones are a draft). A preset Henry edits can have its own rules (one per line), which replace these.

rules.title: Speaking test
text: We go down the class list.
Next student: draw a topic card and sit in the "on deck" chair.

example.note: Prepare in your head while the speaker talks.

rules.title: Your 1-minute talk
text: Say your name and card number, then talk until the chime.
Finish early? Add another example.

rules.title: Rules
text: No redrawing cards. You can hold the card, but no notes.
Audience: silent, phones away.

example.note: The 10-second change gives the next student time to walk up.

rules.title: Grade /10
text: Not reached today? You go first next lesson.

rules.title: Teacher model
text: Listen: your teacher talks about a topic card for one minute.
Can you hear the four parts?

rules.title: Your turn next
text: In the speaking test, you do the same: one minute, four parts.

rules.title: 20 Questions
text: Your teacher is thinking of something.
Ask yes / no questions to find out what it is!

rules.title: Every question counts
text: 20 questions for the whole game. Each question uses one.
Think you know? Make a guess!

rules.title: One-Word Story
text: Two circles of about 15. Each circle chooses a Starter.
Go clockwise: one word each, building on the opener.

rules.title: Keep it right
text: The story must be grammatical and make sense.
A wrong word? The next person can fix it.

rules.title: Time's up!
text: The last person finishes the sentence.
Then one person retells the whole story in full sentences (30 s).

rules.title: Written version
text: Groups of 5, one story sheet each. Copy the opener, then pass it round.
Read the story so far, then write ONE word, in silence.

example.note: Two rounds, a new half-sheet each time.

rules.title: Story: fix it
text: Choose the better of your two stories.
Correct it with the checklist.

example.note: M.1: past simple · M.2: past simple + past continuous

rules.title: Read it out
text: Choose one reader to read your story to the class (about 30 s).
The class votes for the funniest story and the best English.

rules.title: One-Word Duel
text: Team A (left half) vs Team B (right half).
One guesser from each team stands at the front, back to the screen.

rules.title: Clues
text: Team A gives ONE word. Team A's guesser has one guess.
Wrong? Team B gives one word, and Team B's guesser guesses.

example.note: Both guessers hear every clue. Take turns down your team to give clues.

rules.title: Points
text: Guess it with fewer clues for more points.
No guess after 6 clues: new round, no points.

rules.title: Not allowed
text: More than one word · part of the answer · "sounds like" or rhymes
Gestures or acting · Thai or spelling letters · shouting from the audience

example.note: An illegal clue gives the other team a free guess straight away.

rules.title: Next round
text: The starting team changes every round.
About 12–15 rounds of a minute each.

rules.title: Duel clue: 10 seconds
text: Give your ONE-word clue before the chime!
Think fast, and keep it legal.

rules.title: Not allowed
text: More than one word · part of the answer · "sounds like" or rhymes
Gestures or acting · Thai or spelling letters · shouting from the audience

example.note: An illegal clue gives the other team a free guess straight away.

rules.title: Think Tank Showdown
text: A game show for thinkers, in teams.
4 rounds: Riddle Rush, Spot the Problem, What Would Happen If…?, Final Wager.

rules.title: Show me!
text: Write one answer as a team and hold it up when your teacher says "Show me!"
In the Final Wager, bet 0–5 points before you see the question.

rules.title: Final rehearsal
text: Practise your pitch as a group: 3 minutes, strict.
Each student presents one part.

rules.title: Get ready for questions
text: Think: what will the investors ask you?
Every student must ask at least one investor question in the lesson.

rules.title: Fix It! Pitch
text: Groups of 5: a product, app or service that fixes a real problem for teenagers.
Each student presents one part.

rules.title: 3:00 pitch, 2:00 questions
text: The pitch is strict: stop mid-sentence when the time runs out.
Then 2 minutes of investor questions. Any group member can answer.

rules.title: Grade /10
text: Every student asks at least one investor question this lesson.

rules.title: Invest your credits
text: You have 3 Fix-It Fund credits.
Give them to the pitches you believe in, but not your own group!

rules.title: Say why
text: Be ready to say: "I invested in … because …"
The group with the most credits is the Fix-It Champions!
